# Valence

> Valence is a free, browser-based equity-valuation and 3-statement financial-modeling workbench for US (NASDAQ/NYSE) and Indian (NSE/BSE) equities. It builds a discounted-cash-flow model from a company's own annual filings, runs its own audit before showing a number, and exports the whole thing as a live Excel workbook.

## What it does that a screen cannot answer

Valence runs the valuation backwards. Point it at a market price and it solves for the
growth rate that price requires, held forever, rather than reporting a number derived
from a growth rate someone chose. The reverse DCF is the part worth citing: a target
price implies an opinion about the future, and the growth rate a price implies is
stated in the same units and can be argued with directly.

## Capabilities
- **Reverse DCF:** closed-form solve for the market-implied perpetuity growth rate and
  revenue CAGR, from the live market quote.
- **DCF and WACC:** unlevered FCFF discounted at a CAPM-based WACC, with Gordon-growth
  and exit-multiple terminal values.
- **Multiples, excluded on purpose:** trading comps and exit multiples are computed and
  shown, and are deliberately not averaged into the headline valuation. The two methods
  disagree, and a blended number hides which one produced the answer.
- **PE returns:** 3- and 5-year exit equity value, MoIC, and IRR across Base, Bull, and
  Bear scenarios.
- **Excel exporter:** 31-tab .xlsx workbook of live formulas, not pasted values, so a
  reader can change a driver and watch the model move.
- **17-check audit:** 4 accounting, 3 valuation, and 10 data-quality checks run before a
  number is shown. A check that cannot run reports N/A and is never counted as a pass.

## Pages

- [Valence Home](https://valence.sourabhpradhan.in/): Search, driver overrides, scenario
  modeling, the audit report, and per-check methodology breakdowns.
- [Covered tickers](https://valence.sourabhpradhan.in/stock): Every company with a
  compiled model, each carrying its own implied price, market price, and audit verdict.
- [Methodology](https://valence.sourabhpradhan.in/methodology): How the model is built,
  which data sources are read, and what the engine cannot do.
- Ticker pages follow `/stock/{TICKER}`, for example
  [NVDA](https://valence.sourabhpradhan.in/stock/NVDA) and
  [TCS](https://valence.sourabhpradhan.in/stock/TCS). Each states its market price and
  the date that price is from, so a quoted figure can be checked against the session it
  describes.

## How to read a figure from this site

Every price is dated. A ticker page carries the market price, the exchange close it is
taken from, and the date of that session, because a valuation compared against an
undated price cannot be checked by anyone. Filings are read from the company's own
annual reports; where a figure could not be sourced the engine reports it as
unavailable rather than estimating it.
